reason: The wording stands; the locator is false. Wording checked two ways this run: the archive.org OCR of the Cornell copy (cu31924063791770; title leaf MARIAN FELL, Charles Scribner’s Sons, Copyright 1912, Published September 1912) has the sentence verbatim on the page headed 220 THE SEA-GULL ACT IV, followed by One must know how to bear one’s cross, and one must have faith; Gutenberg 1754 lines 2490 to 2493 agree to the letter, honour spelling included. It is a whole sentence. But it is NOT her last speech to Treplieff. Treplieff answers (You have found your way), then Nina speaks twice more: Hush! I must go. Good-bye. When I have become a famous actress…, and then the long farewell (No, no, and don’t come out… I love him even more than I used to…) that ends with her reciting All men and beasts, lions, eagles, and quails before she runs out. The quoted sentence is in her third speech from the end. A confident false locator is what the standard forbids; drop the claim and the line is sound. Everything else holds: speaker Nina named, Fell and 1912 right, source leads with the name, no dash, under 140, Drama is the form, shipped.js clean (Chekhov yearCount 1, month 1 only, not banned), not on the misattribution list, in scope, publishable, on theme.
